quick.topic: Wait for the data, not the clock
quick.summary: Why a job scheduled for six failed when upstream ran late.
quick.takeaway: Start when the input is ready, not at a fixed time.

parts.title: Wait for the data, not the clock

beats.line: My report runs at six. The load finished at ten past. The report was empty. Why?

board.text: Wait for the data, not the clock

beats.line: It trusted the clock. The clock does not know the data is late.
So I move it to seven?
Then one day the load ends at five past seven.
Make the report depend on the load. It starts when the load succeeds.
And if the load fails completely?
Then the report waits, and you get one clear alert. Not an empty report.
Let it try again a few times, with a pause between each.
Report depends on the load. Three more tries, ten minutes apart.
Late data now means a late report, never a wrong one.

quiz.question: A job needs data from an earlier job. How should it be scheduled?
options: To start when the earlier job succeeds
At a fixed time after the earlier job usually ends
An hour later, to be safe
At the same time as the earlier job
quiz.explanation: A dependency starts the job only when its input is really there, however late it is.

quiz.question: Scheduling a job at a fixed time guarantees its input data is ready.
quiz.explanation: The earlier job can run late. Depending on its success starts the job only once that load has finished.
